- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish correction.  
- Model frequently over-estimates short-term spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent high) and under-estimates subsequent pullback; apply a 1–2 day lag correction after sharp rises.  
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.33), model shows mean-reversion bias — forecast too low; adjust upward by 1–3% to capture latent rebound.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently under-forecasts true outcomes by 1–3% in high-sentiment periods; apply a +1.5% bias adjustment when sentiment > 0.67 over last 5 days.  
- Overshoots after spikes (e.g., +10%+ above recent peak) are common; cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak for 2–3 days post-spike.
